entries.statement: AFG continua-manga application: a staged continua table becomes an end-frontier anchor (source 'afg-continua') plus a volume boundary, only after the full gate stack — identity guard, self-consistency, chapter-space gate, episode sanity/conversion, A1 episode type, precedence.
entries.notes: Shared by afg-continua-apply.ts (sweep), canon-tier.ts and refresh-afg (inline upkeep). Each part is also its own entry below.

entries.statement: Continua identity guard: the continua table's heading (normalized) must appear within the series' own names (title, native, search_text, id); otherwise the data is withheld with a parse_integrity flag — AFG's template can name a DIFFERENT series.

where.loc: line 246-249 parseContinua comment (heading captured, never trusted blindly)

entries.notes: norm() strips entities and parenthetical years before comparing.

entries.statement: Continue-from is READING GUIDANCE, not a restatement of the frontier — AFG may legitimately say 'skip ahead' (recap chapters) or 'restart at' (rushed adaptation); only an absurd gap (|continueChapter − 1 − endChapter| > 40) marks the parse suspect and withholds.

where.loc: line 303-305 parseContinua comment ('continueChapter-1 must agree — the apply step's self-consistency gate')

entries.notes: DRIFT: afg.ts comment says continueChapter-1 'must agree' with the frontier; anchors.ts enforces only a 40-chapter tolerance and explicitly says they need not agree.

entries.statement: Chapter-space gate (continua): a continua frontier chapter above max(total_chapters, latest_known_chapters) + 10 is a partial-structure or edition mismatch — withheld with a count_mismatch flag, never written.
entries.notes: Same +10 margin as the chart gate (syncAnchors) and the MU gate (applyMuFrontier). Skipped when the series has no chapter space (spaceMax 0).

entries.statement: AFG episode-numbering conversion: AFG counts in MAL-style numbering, so the claimed frontier episode is shifted past every non-season numbered component (insert) that starts at or before it — unless the page's own chart max already reaches our aired count (already in our space); a converted episode above aired_episodes is discarded and the pin falls back to the run end.
witnesses: Haikyu (Riku vs Kuu = our eps 61-62; AFG ep 85 = our 87)
bundle_parts: walk non-season numbered components, shift past each insert at or before the claimed episode
ep > aired → discard; ep ??= aired_episodes (run-end fallback)
entries.notes: The you-and-i-are-polar-opposites suppression records a case where this conversion landed one episode short of the chart rows ('restructuring-phase gate candidate': cross-check the converted episode against chart rows).

entries.statement: A1 at the AFG continua writer (D4): filler and anime-only rows NEVER take anchors — a continua end-frontier landing on an episode whose type is not canon/mixed is refused with a count_mismatch flag (allow-list, unknown types fail closed; a row-less episode cannot be typed so the pin stands); the continue-from chapter still applies because it is reading guidance, not a position.
entries.notes: Extends D1 (MU writer) to the AFG writers after 49/49 audit hits adjudicated 45 junk / 4 mistyped. Returns 'refused_episode_type'.

entries.statement: Continua precedence at the (series, episode) PK: a manual or wiki anchor at the pin episode is never overwritten (continua cross-checks it — disagreement > 1 chapter files a count_mismatch flag, curated kept); a chart-'afg' or 'mu' anchor yields to the curated continua (disagreement > 2 flags, then continua is applied).
entries.notes: Tier order implied: manual/wiki > afg-continua > afg (chart) / mu. Sources verify each other in conjunction; none limits another.

entries.statement: Parity-continue preservation (C2): continue_chapter/continue_kind/continue_note are curated data that may live on derived rows, so every delete+reinsert rebuild of 'afg' or 'afg-continua' anchors carries them over by episode — otherwise the hourly cron erodes the catalog-wide parity conversion one series at a time.
entries.notes: For continua the continue fields are restored only when the fresh pin lands on the SAME episode as the old one. NOT applied to 'mu' rows (applyMuFrontier deletes without snapshotting continue fields) — possible gap.

entries.statement: Three-numbers model: the explicit continue-from chapter is data of its own (it may skip recaps or backtrack) and is never derived as frontier+1; the continua source owns series.continue_from_chapter ONLY where it owns the frontier — where manual/wiki rule the frontier, research rules the continue point too. Exception: on an A1 refusal the continue-from is still written.
entries.notes: Note the tension: the D4 refusal branch writes continue_from_chapter even though continua did NOT get the frontier — the 'owns it only where it owns the frontier' principle has a stated exception (reading guidance still applies).

entries.statement: Continua volume boundary: written only when absent for (manga, volume); an existing (Wikipedia-staged) boundary that disagrees is not overwritten but files a count_mismatch flag ('verify which edition').
entries.notes: Requires manga_anilist_id and all three of continueVolume/volumeStart/volumeEnd.

entries.statement: AFG numbering alignment: when the AFG page's max episode differs from our max episode by more than 12, the whole page's anchors are withheld with a count_mismatch flag.
entries.notes: Only when we already have episode rows (ourMax truthy). Compares SOURCE-space afgMax against our max BEFORE translation — for shift-ruled series the gap is the insert length (fine under 12).

entries.statement: Chapter-space gate (chart): if any derived AFG chart anchor exceeds max(total_chapters, latest_known_chapters) + 10, the whole page's numbering is suspect (franchise-continuous numbering) — all anchors withheld with a parse_integrity flag, never partially written.
entries.notes: Boruto has 81 chapters; AFG rows said 702-710 (Naruto-space).

entries.statement: Derived-anchor precedence (HxH ep-140 lesson): the PK allows one anchor per episode, so derived 'afg' chart rows at episodes holding a manual/wiki (research-tier) anchor are dropped — curated rows always win on every refresh.
entries.notes: 'completed 2026-08-23'.

entries.statement: Chart anchors translate episode numbers through the source-numbering shifts (space 'afg') exactly like episode rows; dropped order-only entries never anchor.
entries.notes: Also applied to graft annotations. See mashle: AFG numbers are already in our space, so its shift names spaces ['afl'] and this call is a no-op there.

entries.statement: A1 at the AFG chart writer (D4): derived chart anchors on rows typed anything other than canon/mixed are dropped (allow-list; row-less episodes pass) — AFG's chapter column is a reading-position CONVERSION that plateaus across noncanon rows, so a chart value on a noncanon row is a conversion artifact, not an adaptation claim.
witnesses: one-piece (eps 214/216 both print 313 on rows AFG marks *Filler)
entries.notes: Comment names the outcome audit: anchor_on_noncanon_row. The type lookup reads ALL episode rows for the series with an unpaged select — see the 1000-row-cap architecture entry in part 4.

entries.statement: Curated-consistency (Boruto ep-219 lesson): a derived chart row whose chapter contradicts the ordering around any research-tier anchor (chapter above a later curated anchor, or below an earlier one) is chart imprecision — the ruling wins and the derived row drops; ruled rearrangements live as annotations, never as derived rows.
entries.notes: Equal chapter at a different episode is allowed (<= / >=). The 'live as annotations' half is a process statement, not enforced here.

entries.statement: Bonus/fractional chapters a chart associates with an episode are never silently dropped: they become 'graft' episode_annotations, FILL-ONLY (research-tier annotations at the same episode+kind are never clobbered), and set the series' asterisk_review to 'pending' when null.
entries.notes: 'we must always know what content makes up an episode'. A research-verified fractional anchor MAY be written at the manual tier when the bonus IS what the episode adapts.

entries.statement: A successful chart sync registers the afg external id and dismisses every open 'afg' ingest flag for that slug.
entries.notes: Dismisses by series_key = afgSlug and source 'afg' regardless of flag kind.

entries.statement: Volumes-staleness event: when the highest derived anchor chapter passes the last known volume boundary start by more than 20, a 'wikipedia' count_mismatch flag on manga:<id> asks for a volumes re-ingest — the validation tier is event-driven, never scheduled.
entries.notes: Math.max over an empty rows array yields -Infinity, so no flag when nothing was written.

entries.statement: MU's anime-coverage field is multi-segment prose: parse ALL 'Vol N, Chap M' pairs and trust an explicit 'EP N' pin only when the text holds exactly one pair.
witnesses: Naruto (EP number belonging to the Boruto clause)

entries.statement: 'mu' anchors are derivations: applying the MU frontier first DELETES the series' existing 'mu' anchor and re-derives it, so rule fixes heal everything on the next pass; a suppressed series stops after the delete.
entries.notes: Matches CLAUDE.md invariant 7 (repairs on derivation-tier rows are deleted by the next re-derive).

entries.statement: Sibling-scope ceiling (D1): when sibling entries share the same manga, the smallest sibling manga_start_chapter above this entry's own start bounds this entry from above; MU pairs at or past the ceiling are out of scope and filtered; if every in-band pair is past the ceiling the frontier is withheld with a count_mismatch flag (refused_sibling_scope).
entries.notes: The batch-17 franchise-conflation class. Filtering rather than refusing lets the multi-segment parse pick this entry's own labeled endpoint.

entries.statement: MU scope band: only coverage pairs within [manga_start_chapter ?? 1, total_chapters ?? ∞] are candidates; the largest in-scope pair is the coverage.
entries.notes: Scope start comes from series_scopes via manga_start_chapter.

entries.statement: Chapter-space gate (MU pins): MU's coverage prose describes the whole franchise, so a pin above max(total_chapters, latest_known_chapters) + 10 is a structure/edition mismatch — withheld with a count_mismatch flag (out_of_space), never written.

Count-space → number-space conversion (Tokyo Ghoul 144/143): for a finished manga where AniList's total is a COUNT and MU's latest is the last chapter NUMBER (same-edition band: latest < total and latest ≥ 80% of total), an MU pin that lands between them is count-space and is converted to the latest number, so the position never renders coverage above its own denominator; mirrors the display rule in assemble.ts totalChapters exactly.
entries.notes: Writer copy here; display copy in src/data/catalog/assemble.ts totalChapters (client home). The conversion is recorded in the anchor note.

entries.statement: Airing-pin rule (TYBW): without an explicit episode in MU's text the pin would land at the run end, a moving target while airing — so MU frontier pins apply to FINISHED runs only; airing series need the explicit episode or a research anchor.
witnesses: Bleach TYBW (ch 705 announced while part 4 mid-air)
entries.notes: Returns 'no_coverage' silently (no flag). Applies only when the caller passes status; status undefined bypasses the rule.

entries.statement: MU pin episode = the explicit EP when it is ≤ aired_episodes, else the run end (aired_episodes).

MU pin redundancy keys on the PIN EPISODE, never a freshness window or chapter no-progress: the pin is skipped only when a non-MU anchor already covers the pin episode itself (nonMuMaxEp ≥ pin episode).
entries.notes: SUPERSEDES the old 'non-MU anchors within 12 eps of the run end' blanket skip and the chapter no-progress skip (both recorded as pipeline traps in part 4). Rationale: the beyond-frontier display rule refuses to extrapolate past the last anchor, so 'fresh enough' ≠ 'covers the run end'.

entries.statement: Curated precedence at the MU pin episode: any non-'mu' anchor already at the pin episode IS the frontier — the MU pin is skipped (one-anchor-per-episode PK rule).
entries.notes: Broader than manual/wiki: any non-mu source (afg, afg-continua) at the pin episode wins over MU.

entries.statement: Scope-consumed refusal (D1): when non-MU anchors already reach the END of this entry's chapter scope (min(total_chapters, sibling ceiling − 1)) yet the MU pin episode extends beyond all research, the trailing episodes cannot adapt this scope — the frontier is withheld with a count_mismatch flag (refused_scope_consumed); placed after the redundancy skips so a fully-researched series stays a silent skip.
entries.notes: Misses prisma-illya by one chapter (research ENDs stop at 13; 14 is the unadapted epilogue) — hence the MU_FRONTIER_SUPPRESSED entry.

entries.statement: A1 at the MU writer (D1): a run-end MU pin landing on an episode whose type is not canon/mixed is refused with a count_mismatch flag (allow-list; row-less episodes pass so synthesized-row entries keep their frontier); research records the honest terminal on the last canon/mixed episode instead.
entries.notes: The original A1-at-writer gate; D4 (2026-08-25) extended it to both AFG writers.

entries.statement: Same-edition band: MU's latest_chapter is accepted only when 0 < latest < 10000 and, when an AniList count exists, latest ≥ 80% of that count — below the band the two sources track different editions and callers flag, never write.
entries.notes: MU latest_chapter is release-record-derived: reliable for currently scanlated manga, garbage for old completed ones.

entries.statement: Chapter-floor (symmetric to the episode-floor invariant): the chapter space can never be smaller than what confirmed anchors reach — an MU latest below the anchor floor is a different unit space (volumes), never a chapter number, and is rejected.

Best-available latest_known: release-derived latest_chapter first, then the chapter count parsed from MU's status string ('67 Chapters (Ongoing)') as fallback — both behind the same-edition band AND the anchor chapter floor; this is the one derivation every writer uses.
entries.alias: Sean's standing rule (use the best info available)
entries.notes: Consumers: mu-backfill, audit-manga-coverage, apply-rulings-20260825b, refresh-mu.

entries.statement: MU publication status: the explicit completed=true flag wins (finished); else the FIRST line of the status string maps complete→finished, hiatus→hiatus, ongoing→publishing; else completed===false → publishing; else null.
entries.notes: Multi-part status strings state the overall status on line 1.

entries.statement: Manga-status cross-check: MU's publication status is an independent statement; disagreement with our AniList-derived manga_status files a taxonomy_conflict flag for review and NEVER auto-applies; skipped when ours is anime_only or MU has no status.
entries.notes: Catches AniList lag on just-finished manga and the null-totals-but-actually-finished gap.
